summary: The feature's test net is strong and well balanced: every user-spec AC and tech-spec Testing-Strategy item is covered with behaviour-asserting tests (enrollDepth, telegramBotId inheritance, currentStepId, parent status, skip+greppable-WARN, both backstops, re-enter no-op/restart, fail-closed cross-project, return-to-menu, self-target, test-run). Engine-IT is deterministic (MutableClock @Primary local config, JVM-singleton MockWebServer with per-test baseline + drain, Redis rate-key cleanup, explicit engine.sweep()). No critical/major findings. Two minor findings (re-enter no-op logged at INFO not WARN vs AC wording; SUBSCRIBE non_message preview only covered generically via DELAY, not pinned for SUBSCRIBE) plus a couple of info notes. Full suite confirmed green.

highlights: Skip cases assert BOTH the absence of a child execution (childExecution(...) is null / activeChildren size 1) AND the parent reaching completed — not merely 'sweep threw no exception'. Passes the litmus test (removing the skip would create a child / fail the parent).

WARN logs are asserted against greppable constants captured from FunnelEventService via ListAppender at the matching logger — the AC's 'greppable / відстежуваним' requirement is genuinely verified, and each backstop/skip reason uses a DISTINCT constant so the tests cannot pass on the wrong WARN.
fail-closed projectId has a dedicated cross-project target test (subscribeTargetWrongProjectSkipsGracefully) distinct from the missing-target test — both required paths covered, at save and runtime.

enrollDepth is asserted as an exact value (==1, ==3, isZero) everywhere, not just 'enroll happened'. telegramBotId inheritance asserted explicitly against the parent's id. currentStepId asserted to the exact entry/fallback step.

endParentAfter=true asserts BOTH halves (parent completed AND the 'after' step did not send). endParentAfter=false asserts the parallel half (parent 'after' send this tick + child completes next sweep).
test-run delivery is proven by inspecting the RecordedRequest path/chat_id/body, not just a request count.
assertion_quality.weak_or_tautological: None material. The only soft spot is the re-enter no-op log level mismatch (minor-1) and the missing SUBSCRIBE-specific non_message pin (minor-2).

engine_it_determinism.clock: MutableClock (volatile Instant, set/advance) wired @Primary via a LOCAL TestClockConfig @Import so it never leaks into other IT contexts. No Instant.now()/Thread.sleep for timing in any SUBSCRIBE case.
engine_it_determinism.telegram: JVM-singleton MockWebServer; each test measures sends as a delta from a per-test sendBaseline; @BeforeEach resets dispatcher to a fresh QueueDispatcher and @AfterEach drains leftover enqueued responses. FunnelTestRunSendIT explicitly drains its takeRequest() to avoid cross-test queue bleed (the very bug Task 3 review caught).
engine_it_determinism.rate_limit_determinism: GOOD — the rate-limit IT seeds the Redis counter to '1000' directly (seedRateLimitExhausted) and @BeforeEach deletes bf:rate:auto-enroll:* keys, so the backstop trips without any wall-clock wait. The production limiter is a Redis INCR counter with TTL, not a per-minute wall-clock window — no time-based flakiness.
engine_it_determinism.cross_test_state: Mongo (FunnelExecution/Event), subscribers, bots, funnels all wiped @BeforeEach; Redis rate keys cleared. No order dependence observed.
named_flaky_risks: LOW: MockWebServer request log is cumulative across the class; correctness depends on the per-test baseline + the explicit takeRequest() drain in FunnelTestRunSendIT. Already handled, but it is the one structural footgun if a future test forgets to drain.

LOW: subscribeReEnterNoOpWhenTargetInflight seeds the existing child with nextRunAt = BASE + 365 days so the sweep does not claim it mid-tick. Correct, but relies on that far-future value staying outside any clock advance — fine as written.

pyramid_balance.unit: StepTypeTest (enum pin) + FunnelStepExecutorTest (SUBSCRIBE cont/complete + enroll args, all collaborators mocked) — fast, isolated logic where it belongs.
pyramid_balance.integration: Engine-IT (15 SUBSCRIBE cases over real Mongo+Redis+MockWebServer) + FunnelTestRunSendIT (2) + FunnelServiceEmitEventTest save/activation (6) — the runtime/thin-state behaviour correctly tested at integration level (engine claims, depth/rate backstops, fail-closed projectId, re-enter guard all need a real DB).
pyramid_balance.frontend: 6 vitest cases on FunnelStepForm covering render+fetch('all'), submit shape, sentinel→null, non-vacuous inactive hint, entry reset on target switch, edit pre-fill re-emit.
pyramid_balance.e2e: None, as specified (manual Telegram run deferred to user in Task 8).
pyramid_balance.over_under_testing: No over-testing of trivia. No heavy Testcontainers IT used where a unit would do — validation logic that touches the DB is legitimately an IT. Save-validation could in principle be unit-tested with a mocked repo, but the DB-lookup nature makes the IT placement reasonable.

findings.title: Re-enter no-op is logged at INFO, not WARN — user-spec AC literally says 'greppable-WARN'
findings.location: FunnelEventService.java:306 (log.info LOG_ENROLL_REENTER_IGNORED); asserted by FunnelExecutionEngineIT.java:1179 via infoAndWarn(...)
findings.detail: user-spec line 65 and tech-spec Testing-Strategy line 170 phrase the re-enter no-op observability as a greppable WARN; the production code emits it at INFO and the IT therefore asserts it through an info+warn capture rather than warn(...). The AC's underlying intent ('щоб тихе неповернення було відстежуваним' / greppable) IS met — a distinct constant LOG_ENROLL_REENTER_IGNORED is emitted and asserted — so this is a wording/level mismatch, not a coverage hole.
findings.recommendation: Either (a) bump the production log to log.warn to match the AC wording (then tighten the test to warn(appender)), or (b) consciously record in decisions/tech-spec that re-enter no-op is intentionally INFO (it is an expected benign outcome, not an anomaly) and update the AC wording. Test-side change alone is enough to harden the assertion if level stays INFO.

findings.title: non_message preview for SUBSCRIBE_TO_FUNNEL not pinned by a feature test
findings.location: user-spec AC line 67 / tech-spec Testing-Strategy line 157; only generic coverage in FunnelControllerIT.java:797-812 (DELAY → kind=non_message)
findings.detail: The tech-spec asks to assert SUBSCRIBE → non_message placeholder (not in isMessageStep). No SUBSCRIBE-specific assertion exists. isMessageStep is an allow-list so SUBSCRIBE falls through to non_message by construction, and the DELAY IT proves the placeholder path works — but there is no regression pin tying SUBSCRIBE specifically to non_message, so a future accidental addition of SUBSCRIBE to the message allow-list would not be caught.
findings.recommendation: Add a one-line assertion: either a unit assert that previewStep(SUBSCRIBE step).kind == non_message (or !isMessageStep(SUBSCRIBE)), or extend FunnelControllerIT's non_message test to also feed a SUBSCRIBE_TO_FUNNEL step. Cheap, closes the pin gap.

findings.title: 'paused' target runtime-skip not separately seeded
findings.detail: The runtime skip-on-not-active AC names draft AND paused. Only draft is seeded; the production guard is `status != FunnelStatus.active` (a single branch), so draft exercises the exact same code path as paused. Acceptable — adding a paused variant would be redundant per the 'every test earns its place' rule.
findings.recommendation: No action required. Noting for completeness only.

findings.title: Self-target allowReEnter=true restart not separately tested
findings.detail: Only the self-target allowReEnter=false no-op is seeded. The allowReEnter=true self-restart shares the generic insertTargetExecution re-enter branch already covered by subscribeReEnterTrueRestartsTargetFromEntry. tech-spec (Decision/§Self-target) states self behaviour falls out of the re-enter guard with no dedicated code branch, so this is acceptable.

verification.frontend: vitest run tests/pages/funnel-editor.spec.ts → 45 passed (incl. 6 SUBSCRIBE_TO_FUNNEL cases)

overall: clean — no critical or major findings; 2 minor (non-blocking) + 2 info. The test net is ready for pre-deploy QA (Task 8).
